investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-15T03:24–03:31Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected by any check, confirming the pod never started and the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is the direct cause of the pod remaining unscheduled for ~147s before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, the agent VM was never assigned, and the runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-15T03:24–03:31Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the production cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected by any check, confirming the pod never started and the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is the direct cause of the pod remaining unscheduled for ~147s before the eval timed out. Because the pod never started, the agent VM was never assigned, and the runner could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing the expected-output contract to fail completely. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 03:26 and 03:31 UTC on 2026-07-15 because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected by any check, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned and the runtime eval never reached the stage where it could return orgId, agentId, model, provider, or message.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (peer-pod VM slots exhausted), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-carrying nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~145–147 seconds across all three checks, no agent was ever created, no VM became ready, and no runtime response was produced. This is a Kubernetes cluster-capacity or node-affinity configuration problem localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling path in the production-api environment; it is an eval-detected infrastructure failure, not a confirmed user-traffic outage.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource slots are fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all available peer-pod VM quota is in use by existing agents or leaked pods, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests.

[Likely] Node affinity or node selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata-capable nodes), and those nodes are simultaneously at capacity — the 4 remaining nodes are structurally ineligible regardless of their general resource availability.

[Possible] A peer-pod VM or agent pod from a prior eval run was not cleaned up (leaked), holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and preventing new pods from being scheduled on the already-constrained nodes.

[Possible] The cluster was scaled down or a kata-capable node was cordoned, drained, or lost between eval runs, reducing effective VM capacity below the minimum needed to schedule even one new remote agent pod.

[Lower confidence] The node affinity/selector configuration on the remote agent pod spec was recently changed to be more restrictive, shrinking the set of schedulable nodes — however, sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges is empty and no supporting source evidence links any recent change to pod spec affinity rules.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the 2 kata-capable nodes in the production cluster to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm slot utilization and identify which pods are consuming the resource.
Audit the production namespace for any leaked or stuck remote-agent pods (Pending, Running, or Terminating) that may be holding VM slots from prior eval runs and preventing new scheduling.

If slots are exhausted by legitimate workloads, evaluate whether the kata-capable node pool needs to be scaled out (adding nodes or increasing per-node VM quota) to accommodate concurrent eval probes alongside production agent workloads.
If stuck pods are found, force-delete them to release VM slots and re-run the eval suite to confirm recovery.
Review the remote agent pod spec's node affinity and selector to confirm the 4-node exclusion is intentional; if not, correct the affinity rules to expand the schedulable pool.

Monitor the remote-agents feature status after any remediation — the registry sets degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 (infra/evals/status/features.json lines 187-188), so two consecutive required-check failures would trigger an outage signal.

recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Stuck Terminating pods can hold kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without appearing as Running, silently exhausting capacity across eval runs.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the failure, the capacity-exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and a different scheduling or admission-webhook error would need to be investigated.
If the remote-agent-create check passes on a subsequent run without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than a sustained exhaustion or configuration problem.

If the node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec matches all 6 nodes (not just the 2 kata-capable ones), the 4-node affinity mismatch would indicate a node labeling problem rather than a pod spec restriction.

If a sibling check for a different agent type (e.g., local-agent-create) also failed at the same timestamp with a scheduling error, it would suggest a broader cluster scheduling outage rather than a problem specific to the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource or remote-agent node affinity.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots in the production namespace at the time of the failure, the exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a node-level resource reporting bug or admission controller misconfiguration would become more likely.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm slot availability on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing capacity exhaustion as a distinct 'capacity-warn' status rather than a scheduling timeout failure.

Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists all remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL in the production namespace and fails if any are found in Pending or Terminating state, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust VM quota.

Add a node-pool health eval that verifies at least one kata-capable node has a free kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and matches the remote agent pod's node affinity, providing an early warning before any agent creation is attempted.

Introduce a historical pass/fail trend eval for remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime so that the verifier context can populate lastPassingAt and detect regressions from a known-good baseline (currently previousRunCount=0 and lastPassingAt=null, making regression detection impossible).
